one_line_contribution: That per-item credit for retrieved experience is reference-dependent, and that the reference matching the actual decision a memory system makes is not the hole left by leave-one-out but the retriever's next-ranked item backfilling the slot — measured in a multi-step agent (ALFWorld, Qwen3-32B) at ±5 net, with the hole-vs-backfill gap, the gap against a static-exemplar reference, and the additivity error of each reference against realized two-item pruning reported in net points.
closest_prior_work: Two verified threats, at different levels. (i) Setting: CUE-R, arxiv:2604.05467 (verified via s2cli, 2026-04-07, cit 2) already does intervention-based per-evidence utility with REMOVE/REPLACE/DUPLICATE — it is single-shot RAG with distractor replacement, so the specific 'replace with the retriever's own next candidate, in a sequential agent, tied to a pruning decision' move is not made there; that limits but does not remove the threat, since a reviewer will read this as CUE-R's REPLACE arm with a better-chosen replacement. (ii) Concept: the claim that a removal 'hole' is the wrong reference because it is not a plausible state is old and settled in the attribution home literature. arxiv:2110.11929 (verified, 'Double Trouble', AACL 2021, cit 7) shows deletion-metric bias and compares LOO against MLM-synthesized plausible counterfactuals; arxiv:2508.14482 (verified, 2025-08-20) formalizes exactly this as 'semantic missingness' — a baseline must represent a plausible state, not merely absent signal; arxiv:2607.14271 (verified, 2026-07-15) names the reference as one of five specification choices. The proposal cites the latter two but frames them as gaps rather than as the source of its central insight. What survives as new is narrow but real: the reference is chosen not for plausibility but for decision-equivalence (it equals what pruning re-retrieves), and it is evaluated against a downstream sequential outcome rather than a faithfulness metric. That is an incremental specification of a known point, not a new one. I also note arxiv:2605.21768 (Memory-R2, 'Fair Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon Memory-Augmented LLM Agents', 2026-05-20, found via s2cli) which the Related Work does not cite; it is RL training credit rather than counterfactual item value, so it is an omission in coverage rather than a collision.
strongest_objection: The three 'references for the same slot' are not matched on position or set size, so the headline ordering s(H1) < s(S1) < s(B1) confounds reference type with prompt geometry. F = [1,2,3] (new content at position 1, 3 items); H1 = [2,3] (2 items); B1 = [2,3,4] (new content at position 3, 3 items); S1 = [x,2,3] (new content at position 1, 3 items). B1 is a faithful simulation of pruning — that part is right — but the proposal's own prose ('the retriever's next candidate placed in the emptied rank-1 slot') is false: nothing occupies slot 1 in B1, item 2 promotes into it and item 4 appends last. So g_1 = s(B1) − s(H1) is 'what does a third exemplar appended at the end add to a two-item prompt', which mixes the content of item 4 with a set-size/format effect, while sigma_1 = s(S1) − s(H1) gives the static content the primacy slot. Given that position effects in retrieval-augmented prompting are large (the brief's own scan cites arxiv:2605.27105 on position/context-size effects), a reviewer can explain the entire predicted ordering without any claim about references. Second, related: the confirm/falsify bands leave the modal outcome undecided. The proposal's own nested-k prior says items 4–7 add only +2 to +4 net on top of [1,2,3]; P1 predicts item 4 alone adds ≥ +8 on top of a two-item set, and its falsifier requires g_1 ≤ 0 with the CI excluding +8. A measured g_1 of +4 — arguably the most likely value — confirms nothing and falsifies nothing, and the same (0, band) dead zone recurs in P3 (0–12), P4 (0–8) and P5, where the automated entailment check already flagged the falsifier as near-entailed. Third, the title claims 'only backfill predicts what pruning realizes', but the confirmatory arms only realize per-game, one- or two-item pruning from a frozen k=7 log; bank-level pruning, which couples games through shared items and is the decision real systems make, is arm R1, explicitly non-confirmatory and run only if time remains. The headline is therefore not tested at the granularity it claims.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a position-matched backfill arm B1_pos = [4,2,3] (item 4 promoted into slot 1) alongside B1 = [2,3,4], and/or a position-matched static arm S1_end = [2,3,x]; report g_1 and sigma_1 with the position factor crossed, so the reference claim is separated from prompt geometry. This is one extra 1,644-episode arm (~82 min) and the budget already has headroom. (2) Re-band the predictions so the likely outcome decides them: state P1 as a two-sided partition (confirm g_1 ≥ +6, falsify g_1 ≤ +2 by TOST against ±3 versus zero) rather than confirm ≥ +8 / falsify ≤ 0, and do the same for P3, P4 and P5 (the entailment check's fix for P5 — falsifier at g_1' ≤ 0 or TOST on g_1 − g_1' against ±3 — should be applied to all four). (3) Promote R1 (prune every validation rank-1 item from the bank, re-retrieve) from leftover-time fidelity check to a confirmatory arm with a pre-registered equivalence margin on s(B1) − s(R1), or retitle the paper to claim per-game pruning only. (4) Credit the removal-based-explanation literature explicitly (arxiv:2110.11929, arxiv:2508.14482) and state the delta as decision-equivalence of the reference, not as the discovery that references matter.
missing_baseline: A content-controlled third-item reference: a random or bank-matched irrelevant item (or a duplicate of item 2, i.e. CUE-R's DUPLICATE) placed in the same position as the backfill item, token-matched. Without it, g_1 cannot distinguish 'the retriever's next candidate specifically carries +8 net' from 'any third exemplar restores the three-shot format the reader expects', which is the cheapest alternative explanation of P1 and hence of the headline P3. The proposal has token-matched placebos everywhere else (static within 15%, wrong-procedure within 5%) but leaves precisely the arm carrying its mechanism unplacebo'd. A secondary omission: no leave-one-out at any slot other than rank 1 and rank 2 outside the pairwise arm, so the 'slot property' assertion in the hypothesis is never checked at a second slot.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this round — four queries, channel named for each, IDs given, negative results reported as negative rather than as evidence — and it is right that nothing in the agent-memory or RAG literature makes this claim. But it is incomplete on the axis where the idea actually comes from: its 'home' query used feature-attribution vocabulary yet returned only baseline-taxonomy papers, missing the empirical NLP work that already shows LOO disagreeing with plausible-replacement references. My queries (all channel (a) s2cli, S2+HF both ok; WebSearch unavailable this session): 'counterfactual reference for removing a retrieved item: hole versus replacement by next-ranked candidate' --recent → 8 hits, nothing on the claim (arxiv:2604.05467, arxiv:2608.22856, arxiv:2506.20854); 'leave-one-out estimate overstates the effect of deleting a document because the retriever backfills the slot' → 12 hits, all unlearning / KV-eviction / LOO-distinguishability (arxiv:2309.17310, arxiv:2502.15082), nothing on retrieval backfill; 'CUE-R intervention-based per-evidence utility remove replace duplicate retrieval-augmented generation' → arxiv:2604.05467, arxiv:2605.01302 (CoRM-RAG), arxiv:2608.23252 (causal context allocation) — none uses the next-ranked candidate as reference; 'choice of baseline reference value in removal-based feature attribution changes the ranking of inputs' → arxiv:2110.11929, arxiv:1910.04256, arxiv:2402.09164; 'input marginalization plausible replacement versus zero baseline deletion metric text explanation' → arxiv:2110.11929 (AACL, cit 7), arxiv:2412.17512 (BEE, learned baselines); 'pruning a memory bank item is backfilled by the next retrieved item so per-item utility mis-estimates the pruning effect' --recent → empty (2 irrelevant hits); 'data valuation removal of a training point versus replacement reference in retrieval corpora downstream decision' --recent → empty (5 irrelevant hits); 'per-item credit assignment for experience memory in LLM agents validated by ablating memory items ALFWorld' --recent → 12 agent-memory papers (arxiv:2605.21768 Memory-R2, arxiv:2607.21106 AttriMem, arxiv:2605.04811 TreeMem, arxiv:2603.04549 A-MAC, arxiv:2601.08435 Fine-Mem), none validating a per-item score against a counterfactual. ID verification: VERIFIED arxiv:2604.05467 (2026-04-07, cit 2), arxiv:2507.04480 (2025-07-06, PKDD/ECML Workshops, cit 7), arxiv:2607.14271 (2026-07-15, cit 1), arxiv:2508.14482 (2025-08-20), arxiv:2606.29502 (2026-06-28, cit 9), arxiv:2512.10696 (2025-12-11), arxiv:2607.22562 (2026-05-29, cit 1), arxiv:2605.04811 and arxiv:2605.01302 (both returned by search). COULD NOT VERIFY: arxiv:2509.12765 (DIG confidence gain) — not found on S2 or HF; it is load-bearing in the Related Work as one of the three hole-based estimators, and it is also the id the brief carries, so both should be re-checked. arxiv:2606.16285, arxiv:2605.30712 and arxiv:2603.05093 were not checked. Net: the collision check is a genuine search, not a formality, but it establishes novelty only against the agent/RAG axis; against the attribution-baseline axis the point is prior art, and the proposal should be scored on the decision-equivalence delta alone.
